one_liner: Project manager in NNSA's nuclear nonproliferation office, running budgets, plans, metrics and relationships with national labs, contractors and international partners to keep dangerous nuclear materials out of adversaries' hands.
fit_summary: Daniel's M.A. in Global Affairs fits a foreign affairs job, and his coordination with federal, state and private-sector clients fits the partnering side. The gap is the specialized experience at GS-12/NQ-02 level: international engagement, foreign or interagency coordination and national security or foreign policy work, which his domestic emergency management and public health resume doesn't show.
eligibility: Open to the public, so no prior federal status is needed and Daniel can apply as a U.S. citizen.

At least one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-12/NQ-02, supporting U.S. national security and foreign policy objectives through international engagement, foreign and domestic stakeholder coordination, and program execution.

0130 basic requirement, met in one of three ways: a degree or 24 semester hours in political science, international relations, history, economics or a related field; a qualifying education-plus-experience combination; or four years of foreign-affairs-related experience.
Must be able to obtain and keep a Q Access Authorization, DOE's top-level clearance, which involves an extensive background investigation.
Must pass the USA Hire Assessment cut score to be considered at all.
keywords: recommendations and expert advice to senior leadership
strategy: Apply in the October 29 to November 5, 2026 window, which is only about one week, and have your two-page resume and unofficial transcripts ready before it opens.
Upload his George Mason transcript: an M.A. in Global Affairs fits 'international relations or a related field' for the 0130 education requirement, the cleanest route.

Frame your IEM work as program execution for government clients, covering budgets, project plans, metrics, contractor coordination and multi-agency stakeholder work, using whatever you actually did. Highlight any federal, DHS/FEMA, interagency or international work explicitly.
For each relevant job, state dates, hours per week and GS-12-level complexity, such as scope, dollar amounts, number of partners and senior-level briefings. Keep the whole resume within two pages.
Answer the application questionnaire honestly. Claim expert-level answers only where your resume backs them up, because overstating can remove you from consideration.
Prepare for the USA Hire Assessment by taking it in one quiet sitting. It tests judgment, teamwork, stress tolerance and reading comprehension.
resume_bullets: Served as on-site assistant to project managers on multi-state COVID-19 operations (2021–2022).
Studied global trade relations and economic globalization for an M.A. in Global Affairs (George Mason, 2016).
interview_questions: Tell us about a project where you managed a budget, schedule and metrics across multiple contractors or partners.
Describe a time you built a working relationship with a stakeholder whose priorities differed from yours.
What experience do you have with international partners or interagency coordination on national security issues?
How would you brief a senior leader on a program that is falling behind plan?
watch_outs: The specialized experience requires international and national security work, and his IEM work was domestic, so he may be rated not qualified.
A Q clearance is required. Investigations take months and examine finances, foreign contacts and drug use.
The application window is roughly one week, the job has no telework, and it requires an in-person DC commute from Manassas plus some travel.
Upload his transcript: an M.A. in Global Affairs should meet any 0130 coursework requirement, but compare it with the posting's list.
